description: We are Team NASHA, a multidisciplinary team of three developers and researchers passionate about artificial intelligence, space exploration, and scientific discovery. With experience in AI, machine learning, software development, and collaborative research, we aim to leverage open scientific data and emerging technologies to develop innovative, practical, and impactful solutions. We value curiosity, creativity, interdisciplinary collaboration, and learning through exploration.
summary:
Mars BEACON: Every Step on Mars Needs a Way Home.

Mars BEACON is an interactive 3D Martian exploration and mission-planning platform that transforms NASA's planetary data into actionable insights for future human exploration.

Developed for the Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map challenge, it combines high-resolution HiRISE terrain, Curiosity rover observations, AI-assisted terrain analysis, and environmental data into a unified digital exploration environment centered on Mount Sharp's boxwork formations in Gale crater.

Its defining innovation, the 'Return Envelope', calculates terrain-aware return feasibility for two astronauts using oxygen, mission time, cooling-water, battery budgets, and configurable safety reserves. Users can compare scientific routes, investigate geological features, and rehearse missions through seven interconnected operational views, including Mission Control, EVA, and rover perspectives.

The platform also integrates rover-image segmentation, experimental 3D spatial reconstruction, historical radiation observations, weather context, and interactive route visualization. Scientific observations, derived results, and scenario assumptions remain explicitly distinguished.

Mars BEACON demonstrates how planetary mapping can evolve into an intelligent, human-centered decision-support system, making future Mars exploration more informed, resource-aware, and scientifically accessible.
details:
Mars BEACON: Every Step on Mars Needs a Way Home

Mars BEACON is an interactive, browser-based Mars exploration planning and mission rehearsal platform developed by Team NASHA for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It addresses a critical challenge of human exploration on Mars: how can astronauts explore scientifically valuable terrain while ensuring they retain sufficient resources to return safely?

Unlike conventional planetary maps that primarily visualize terrain, Mars BEACON combines real NASA and USGS geospatial data, AI-assisted terrain analysis, environmental observations, and resource-aware path planning into a unified mission-support interface.

How It Works

Our primary study area is a 3 × 3 km region of Mount Sharp's boxwork terrain in Gale crater. Using Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter HiRISE elevation models and imagery, we construct an interactive 3D Martian environment. Additional datasets from Curiosity, NASA Mars Trek, REMS, RAD, and DONKI provide geological, environmental, and space-weather context.

Our central innovation is the Return Envelope, a terrain-aware planning system that calculates which locations remain reachable while preserving a feasible return route to a habitat or designated support-rover haven.

Instead of relying on a simple distance radius, the system considers terrain difficulty, astronaut movement speed, oxygen consumption, cooling-water and battery budgets, mission duration, and configurable safety reserves. It models two astronauts sharing a route, with movement constrained by the slower crew member and resources evaluated separately for each suit.

Astronauts and mission planners can:

  • Explore real Martian terrain through an interactive 3D map.
  • Compare science-focused, balanced, and safety-margin-focused routes.
  • Visualize terrain slope, roughness, potential obstacles, and geological features.
  • Adjust astronaut equipment loads, movement speeds, mission duration, and resource budgets.
  • Observe how the Return Envelope changes as mission conditions change.
  • Rehearse missions through interconnected Habitat, Mission Control, Tablet, EVA, Visor, Rover, and Linked interfaces.
  • Examine rover imagery, terrain-classification results, and experimental spatial reconstructions.
  • Export routes and mission information for further analysis.

Scientific Data and AI Integration

Mars BEACON integrates NASA/USGS HiRISE elevation and image products, Curiosity rover observations, AI4Mars terrain-classification data, REMS atmospheric measurements, RAD historical radiation observations, and space-weather information from DONKI.

Our machine-learning pipeline supports rover-image terrain segmentation and derived terrain analysis. Experimental 3D reconstruction explores how local rover observations might complement orbital perspectives. A separate Jezero crater demonstration shows how the site-processing pipeline can be reused.

Technology Stack

The application was developed using React, TypeScript, Three.js, React Three Fiber, Zustand, Vite, and browser Web Workers. The backend uses Python, FastAPI, and SQLite/PostgreSQL. Offline scientific processing and machine-learning workflows use Python-based geospatial and AI tools.

The primary route-planning engine uses a terrain-aware graph-search approach operating on a 4 m planning grid. Browser-side processing allows interactive route evaluation without requiring a continuous backend connection.

Creativity and Innovation

Mars BEACON's distinguishing feature is its integration of planetary mapping with human-centered mission decision-making.

Rather than presenting isolated scientific datasets, we connect terrain, environmental context, crew resources, science opportunities, and return-route feasibility within one interactive system. Multiple mission displays share a consistent state, allowing users to examine the same exploration scenario from different operational perspectives.

The design emphasizes scientific traceability, interactive exploration, and clear communication of uncertainty. Observational data, derived information, scenario assumptions, and experimental outputs are distinguished rather than presented as equally certain.

Intended Impact

Mars BEACON demonstrates how real planetary datasets can support more understandable, resource-conscious planning for future human exploration. It also provides an educational platform for exploring the challenges of astronaut mobility, planetary geology, robotics, and autonomous mission operations.

Our current implementation is a research and hackathon prototype, not a certified astronaut-safety system. The Return Envelope represents feasibility under documented assumptions, not guaranteed mission safety. Future work includes stronger model validation, improved obstacle detection, uncertainty estimation, and more detailed rover-to-orbital reconstruction.

Live Platform: https://mars-beacon.pages.dev/

Source Code: https://github.com/Harishik/Mars-Beacon
